world.title: Brazil court orders Meta to ensure equal treatment before runoff
world.summary: Internal messages reviewed by Brazilian newspaper Folha de S.Paulo show that Meta employees acknowledged restrictions that hindered President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s Instagram accounts during Brazil’s election campaign, while the platform recommended challenger Flávio Bolsonaro’s profile and WhatsApp channel. The m
world.content: Internal messages reviewed by Brazilian newspaper Folha de S.Paulo show that Meta employees acknowledged restrictions that hindered President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s Instagram accounts during Brazil’s election campaign, while the platform recommended challenger Flávio Bolsonaro’s profile and WhatsApp channel. The messages discussed technical failures and their severity; they did not show an admission of deliberate political interference. Brazil’s top electoral court ordered Meta on Thursday to apply identical standards to both candidates’ political content, searches and AI-generated material or face a daily fine of 500,000 reais. The judge said there was not yet enough evidence to conclude that Meta deliberately manipulated distribution. Meta attributed the problems to technical glitches and denied favoring either side; Lula’s campaign said it would take its complaint to international bodies. Lula and Bolsonaro are due to face each other in a runoff on October 25.

world.title: Carney makes final Alberta appeal as vote on separation process nears
world.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney made a final appeal Friday in Edmonton for Alberta to remain in Canada, ahead of Monday’s vote on whether to start the legal process for a future separation referendum. The Oct. 19 ballot is not a direct vote on independence. Carney warned that a vote against Canada could bring years
world.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney made a final appeal Friday in Edmonton for Alberta to remain in Canada, ahead of Monday’s vote on whether to start the legal process for a future separation referendum. The Oct. 19 ballot is not a direct vote on independence. Carney warned that a vote against Canada could bring years of uncertainty and urged voters not to assume the result was settled. Carney’s final stop followed campaigning in Calgary and a Friday appearance in Red Deer alongside Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, who also opposes separation. Smith has backed the ballot’s nine other proposals, while Carney urged voters to reject them. President Donald Trump has threatened to make Canada the 51st U.S. state, and the two countries are in a trade dispute.
world.image_alt: Carney makes final Alberta appeal as vote on separation process nears

world.title: UK police assess post on banned group by national security adviser
world.summary: London's Metropolitan Police said they are assessing an Oct. 15 post by journalist and author Sarah Helm, wife of UK National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell, that expressed support for Palestine Action, which Britain has proscribed under terrorism law. Police said they are deciding whether to investigate; they have n
world.content: London's Metropolitan Police said they are assessing an Oct. 15 post by journalist and author Sarah Helm, wife of UK National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell, that expressed support for Palestine Action, which Britain has proscribed under terrorism law. Police said they are deciding whether to investigate; they have not announced an investigation. Helm was responding to debate over Irish novelist Sally Rooney, who said she would stop UK sales of her books after publisher Faber concluded that transferring royalties to Palestine Action could expose it to criminal liability. Under the ban, expressing support for the group can be a criminal offence carrying a maximum 14-year prison sentence. Downing Street said Helm's views do not represent the government, while the Supreme Court is due to hear an appeal against the ban next month.
world.image_alt: UK police assess post on banned group by national security adviser

world.title: Indian police arrest youth movement founder after Delhi voter-roll protests
world.summary: Indian police detained Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), on Friday, Oct. 16, as he headed to a Delhi rally demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Indian media reported on Saturday that he had been formally arrested to prevent a breach of the peace. Hundred
world.content: Indian police detained Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), on Friday, Oct. 16, as he headed to a Delhi rally demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Indian media reported on Saturday that he had been formally arrested to prevent a breach of the peace. Hundreds gathered in central New Delhi despite the police presence and the closure of the planned protest site. The demonstrations have focused on a voter-roll revision that removed more than 130 million names, which protesters say unfairly benefits Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). India’s Election Commission denies political bias and says the revision removed deceased, relocated or duplicate voters, while the BJP says its opponents are undermining legitimate electoral processes. Police also detained Neha Bora, president of the All India Students’ Association, who was later released. Dipke was due to appear before a Special Executive Magistrate on Saturday, according to his party’s legal affairs head and Indian media reports.
world.image_alt: Indian police arrest youth movement founder after Delhi voter-roll protests

world.title: Trump denies ordering Ukraine satellite curbs as sources point to White House
world.summary: President Donald Trump on Friday denied ordering restrictions on Ukraine’s military satellite communications, saying neither he nor SpaceX chief Elon Musk was responsible. Ukrainian forces had reported service disruptions, and Reuters sources cited in several reports said the order came from the White House. Trump also
world.content: President Donald Trump on Friday denied ordering restrictions on Ukraine’s military satellite communications, saying neither he nor SpaceX chief Elon Musk was responsible. Ukrainian forces had reported service disruptions, and Reuters sources cited in several reports said the order came from the White House. Trump also said he was unsure whether the service had been interrupted. The system at issue is Starshield, the military service built on SpaceX’s Starlink satellite network. Ukrainian personnel said speed limits caused drones to lose connections, disrupted military communications and led to failed missions. The reported limits changed over several days, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in Brussels on Friday that service had improved but was not fully restored. Washington had warned it could withhold intelligence if Ukraine continued attacking Russian oil refineries and was pushing for an energy ceasefire. At a Brussels summit, Zelensky asked the European Union for at least €70 billion for Ukraine’s defense next year. French President Emmanuel Macron said European countries were working to help with satellite and early-warning systems.
world.image_alt: Trump denies ordering Ukraine satellite curbs as sources point to White House

world.title: Yemen
world.summary: Two missiles struck the grounds of Aden International Airport in southern Yemen late Friday. The Houthi movement later said it had targeted a Saudi forces command headquarters and a nearby weapons depot. No casualties were reported. A Yemenia Airways flight to Cairo was preparing to take off; Yemen's information minist
world.content: Two missiles struck the grounds of Aden International Airport in southern Yemen late Friday. The Houthi movement later said it had targeted a Saudi forces command headquarters and a nearby weapons depot. No casualties were reported. A Yemenia Airways flight to Cairo was preparing to take off; Yemen's information minister said the missiles landed about 500 metres from the aircraft and that passengers and crew were safe. The strike was the second at the airport in less than 10 days and followed a Houthi attack on an Aden palace complex on Thursday that killed at least five people. Aden is the seat of Yemen's internationally recognized government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia. The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting a missile headed for Yanbu and destroying other missiles and drones, while fighting intensified elsewhere in Yemen. Brent crude briefly reached $110 a barrel, its highest level since May, as regional security concerns raised worries about oil supplies.

world.title: Brazil records lowest Amazon deforestation on record as election runoff approaches
world.summary: Brazil’s Amazon rainforest lost 3,335 square kilometres of forest from August 2025 through July 2026, down 41.8% from the previous year and the lowest annual total since records began in 1988, official satellite data show. The rate has fallen 71.2% since 2022, the year before President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva took of
world.content: Brazil’s Amazon rainforest lost 3,335 square kilometres of forest from August 2025 through July 2026, down 41.8% from the previous year and the lowest annual total since records began in 1988, official satellite data show. The rate has fallen 71.2% since 2022, the year before President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva took office. The government credits stronger monitoring, enforcement and funding for environmental agencies. Lula revived the Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of Deforestation in the Legal Amazon, a program first launched in 2004 and shelved under his predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro. The government released the figures ahead of the October 25 presidential runoff between Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who finished first in the October 4 vote with 47% to Lula’s 45%. Lula aims to end illegal deforestation by 2030, while Bolsonaro has pledged to end it by 2029 and has called for environmental laws to be modernized.
world.image_alt: Brazil records lowest Amazon deforestation on record as election runoff approaches

world.title: Mexican court sentences three men to 158 years for surfers’ murders
world.summary: A judge in Ensenada sentenced each of three Mexican men to 158 years and nine months in prison on Oct. 16 for murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their American friend Jack Carter Rhoad during a 2024 surf trip in Baja California. The men — Jesús Gerardo García, known as “El Kekas,” Irineo Francis
world.content: A judge in Ensenada sentenced each of three Mexican men to 158 years and nine months in prison on Oct. 16 for murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their American friend Jack Carter Rhoad during a 2024 surf trip in Baja California. The men — Jesús Gerardo García, known as “El Kekas,” Irineo Francisco and Ángel Jesús — had been found guilty a week earlier of homicide and offenses related to violent robbery. Prosecutors said the attackers tried to steal the tires from the surfers’ pickup truck and killed the three men when they resisted. The victims were camping near Punta San José on April 27, 2024; their bodies were found on May 3 in a well more than 15 meters deep. The prosecution had sought 210 years for each defendant. The families can pursue compensation through civil proceedings after the judge rejected the prosecution’s request for damages, The Guardian reported. The defense has indicated it will appeal and has 10 days to file, according to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation.
world.image_alt: Mexican court sentences three men to 158 years for surfers’ murders

business.title: China proposes export bans and curbs on 40 strategic technologies
business.summary: China has proposed banning exports of 14 technologies and restricting another 26 in a draft covering artificial intelligence, semiconductors, solar power and biotechnology. The plan would expand Beijing’s controls on sensitive technology transfers as Chinese companies grow more competitive in several of the affected se
business.content: China has proposed banning exports of 14 technologies and restricting another 26 in a draft covering artificial intelligence, semiconductors, solar power and biotechnology. The plan would expand Beijing’s controls on sensitive technology transfers as Chinese companies grow more competitive in several of the affected sectors. China’s Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology issued the draft, citing national security, the prevention of misuse and the need to keep AI under human control. A one-month public consultation began Friday, Oct. 16.

business.title: Carney urges Alberta to reject separation process before Monday vote
business.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney urged Albertans to reject a ballot measure that would begin the legal process toward a future separation referendum. The vote is scheduled for Monday, Oct. 19. More than 450,000 people had already voted early or by mail, and Carney held a unity rally in Calgary on Thursday before a s
business.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney urged Albertans to reject a ballot measure that would begin the legal process toward a future separation referendum. The vote is scheduled for Monday, Oct. 19. More than 450,000 people had already voted early or by mail, and Carney held a unity rally in Calgary on Thursday before a second event in Edmonton on Friday. Carney linked unity to economic resilience as U.S. President Donald Trump’s trade dispute with Canada and threats to make Canada the 51st state continue. Separatists argue Ottawa has constrained Alberta’s oil and gas development and that independence would leave the province with more of its wealth; opponents warn separation could bring billions of dollars in debt and drive away jobs and investment. Alberta Premier Danielle Smith, who called the vote but supports remaining in Canada, also put nine other questions on the ballot, including questions about provincial control of immigration. Carney urged voters to reject those measures as well.
business.image_alt: Carney urges Alberta to reject separation process before Monday vote

business.title: CoreWeave sell-off spotlights debt risks in AI infrastructure boom
business.summary: Shares in CoreWeave, a cloud provider that rents out computing power powered by Nvidia processors, swung sharply this week as investors focused on its borrowing costs rather than a sudden drop in demand for artificial intelligence computing. The company has about $50 billion in debt, and its losses have raised question
business.content: Shares in CoreWeave, a cloud provider that rents out computing power powered by Nvidia processors, swung sharply this week as investors focused on its borrowing costs rather than a sudden drop in demand for artificial intelligence computing. The company has about $50 billion in debt, and its losses have raised questions about whether AI revenue can justify the industry’s heavy infrastructure spending. CoreWeave shares rebounded 5% on Thursday after falling as much as 8.3% to their lowest level since May 2025. The yield on bonds it issued in April was around 15%, while the cost of insuring its debt against default rose to about 1,000 basis points. CEO Mike Intrator told employees the company’s backlog of deals more than covers its debt obligations.
business.image_alt: CoreWeave sell-off spotlights debt risks in AI infrastructure boom

business.title: Apple
business.summary: Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, sold out its initial pre-order batch within minutes on Friday, pushing estimated delivery dates for new orders into late January 2027. The $1,999 phone is scheduled to begin reaching customers on Oct. 23. By Friday, Apple’s store showed Jan. 25 delivery estimates for a
business.content: Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, sold out its initial pre-order batch within minutes on Friday, pushing estimated delivery dates for new orders into late January 2027. The $1,999 phone is scheduled to begin reaching customers on Oct. 23. By Friday, Apple’s store showed Jan. 25 delivery estimates for all configurations, with some customers seeing Jan. 29. The delay reflects both strong early demand and limited initial supply, but Apple has not disclosed how many orders it received. The Duo has a 5.4-inch outer screen and unfolds to reveal a 7.6-inch display designed for multitasking. The phone starts at $1,999 and is scheduled to launch Oct. 23.

business.title: Social Security sets 3.6% increase for 2027, adding about $75 a month
business.summary: Social Security benefits will rise 3.6% in January 2027, adding an average of about $75 a month for retirees and affecting roughly 72 million recipients. The adjustment reflects inflation and is higher than this year's 2.8% increase. The raise is the largest in four years, though below the 8.7% adjustment announced in
business.content: Social Security benefits will rise 3.6% in January 2027, adding an average of about $75 a month for retirees and affecting roughly 72 million recipients. The adjustment reflects inflation and is higher than this year's 2.8% increase. The raise is the largest in four years, though below the 8.7% adjustment announced in 2022. It is also 0.9 percentage points above Social Security trustees' recent projection. The retirement trust fund that pays benefits is projected to run short in late 2032. Military retirees are also expected to receive a 3.6% pension increase in 2027.
business.image_alt: Social Security sets 3.6% increase for 2027, adding about $75 a month

business.title: MSCI proposes Indonesia’s removal from emerging-market indexes by 2027
business.summary: MSCI, the global index provider, has proposed reclassifying Indonesia from an emerging market to a standalone market, a move that could force index-tracking funds to sell Indonesian shares. The proposal followed investor concerns about opaque shareholding structures, suspected coordinated trading and weak enforcement;
business.content: MSCI, the global index provider, has proposed reclassifying Indonesia from an emerging market to a standalone market, a move that could force index-tracking funds to sell Indonesian shares. The proposal followed investor concerns about opaque shareholding structures, suspected coordinated trading and weak enforcement; MSCI said reforms have not yet produced consistent, material improvements. Indonesia’s Jakarta Composite Index fell about 11% on Oct. 16, its steepest daily drop since 1998, while the rupiah weakened. The change would bypass the frontier-market category and remove Indonesian stocks from MSCI’s main emerging- and frontier-market groupings. MSCI is accepting feedback through April 30, 2027, and expects to decide by the end of June unless it sees clear evidence of improved market governance and functioning. Indonesia’s stock exchange says it will seek clarification and cites steps taken to improve transparency and integrity. The selloff followed billions of dollars in foreign investor withdrawals from Indonesian equities this year, as the benchmark index and rupiah weakened.
business.image_alt: MSCI proposes Indonesia’s removal from emerging-market indexes by 2027

business.title: Trump suspends Russia energy sanctions before 100% tariffs take effect
business.summary: President Donald Trump on Friday, Oct. 16, waived sanctions and tariffs under a law he signed last month to pressure Russia over its war in Ukraine. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act would have allowed duties of up to 100% on goods from major buyers of Russian oil and gas, along with penalties targe
business.content: President Donald Trump on Friday, Oct. 16, waived sanctions and tariffs under a law he signed last month to pressure Russia over its war in Ukraine. The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act would have allowed duties of up to 100% on goods from major buyers of Russian oil and gas, along with penalties targeting Russian officials, banks and oil tankers used to evade restrictions. Trump said the waiver was in the U.S. national interest, but the executive order did not explain why. The waiver remains in effect until he or senior officials decide further action is appropriate. The move followed a diesel supply agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin that Trump said would bring Russian fuel to global markets and help ease rising prices. The waiver came days before the law’s measures were due to take effect.
business.image_alt: Trump suspends Russia energy sanctions before 100% tariffs take effect

business.title: Brent crude settles near $110 as supply disruptions deepen
business.summary: Brent crude futures settled at $109.86 a barrel on Friday, Oct. 16, after briefly reaching $110 for the first time since May. U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 3.5% to $101.41. Brent gained 4.9% for the week and WTI 10.4%, as traders priced in fresh risks to Middle East exports and uncertainty over Russian diesel
business.content: Brent crude futures settled at $109.86 a barrel on Friday, Oct. 16, after briefly reaching $110 for the first time since May. U.S. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) rose 3.5% to $101.41. Brent gained 4.9% for the week and WTI 10.4%, as traders priced in fresh risks to Middle East exports and uncertainty over Russian diesel supplies. Iranian attacks around the Strait of Hormuz intensified, while Iran-backed Houthi forces struck Saudi Arabia and a Saudi-led coalition intercepted a missile headed toward the Red Sea port of Yanbu. Crude shipments through Hormuz fell to 9.4 million barrels a day in the week ending Oct. 14, about 70% of their prewar average, according to energy-data firm Kpler. The International Energy Agency (IEA) agreed to release more than 20 million barrels of fuel, and the U.S. Department of Energy sought an exchange of up to 17 million barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. A proposed U.S.-Russia diesel arrangement faces opposition in Congress as Ukraine resumed strikes on Russian energy sites. The IEA expects diesel inventories to remain depleted until the second half of 2027.
business.image_alt: Brent crude settles near $110 as supply disruptions deepen

science.title: Astronomers identify green white dwarf and unusually red stellar remnant
science.summary: Astronomers have identified a white dwarf, WD J1330+6435, whose light would appear green to human eyes, according to a study published Oct. 15 in RAS Techniques and Instruments. Researchers inferred the color from the star’s spectrum rather than observing it directly; they say it is the first known genuinely green star
science.content: Astronomers have identified a white dwarf, WD J1330+6435, whose light would appear green to human eyes, according to a study published Oct. 15 in RAS Techniques and Instruments. Researchers inferred the color from the star’s spectrum rather than observing it directly; they say it is the first known genuinely green star. White dwarfs are the dense, cooling cores left after low- or medium-mass stars exhaust their fuel. Researchers analyzed 151 white dwarfs within 65 light-years of Earth and found that about one in 30 would appear a color other than white. In the green star, sodium in the dense helium atmosphere absorbs orange light, leaving a green hue. Lead researcher Mark Hollands, an astronomer at the University of Warwick, plans to study more white-dwarf spectra as new surveys expand the available data.
science.image_alt: Astronomers identify green white dwarf and unusually red stellar remnant

science.title: UN biodiversity review warns 2030 protection targets remain out of reach
science.summary: A United Nations review says fewer than half of assessed national biodiversity targets are on track, and current commitments would protect only 26% of terrestrial ecosystems and 12% of marine ecosystems by 2030, below the global goal of 30%. Delegates from nearly 200 countries are due to begin the COP17 biodiversity co
science.content: A United Nations review says fewer than half of assessed national biodiversity targets are on track, and current commitments would protect only 26% of terrestrial ecosystems and 12% of marine ecosystems by 2030, below the global goal of 30%. Delegates from nearly 200 countries are due to begin the COP17 biodiversity conference in Yerevan on Monday to review progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. The framework, agreed in 2022, set targets for reversing nature loss by 2030, but the review identifies shortfalls in finance, technical capacity, cooperation and data. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres said biodiversity funding remains below half of the framework’s $200 billion annual goal; he also cited $7.3 trillion that flowed to industries that harm nature in 2023. Governments are not expected to make major new pledges at COP17, but face pressure to address the gaps.
science.image_alt: UN biodiversity review warns 2030 protection targets remain out of reach

science.title: CERN and Mistral plan an AI foundation model for particle physics
science.summary: CERN, the European particle-physics research organization, and Mistral AI, an artificial intelligence company, have formed a long-term strategic partnership to develop a foundation model for scientific discovery, including particle physics. The project focuses on particle physics. The model is intended to replace some
science.content: CERN, the European particle-physics research organization, and Mistral AI, an artificial intelligence company, have formed a long-term strategic partnership to develop a foundation model for scientific discovery, including particle physics. The project focuses on particle physics. The model is intended to replace some specialized algorithms used to reconstruct and identify particles in particle-collision data.
science.image_alt: CERN and Mistral plan an AI foundation model for particle physics

science.title: Global timekeepers abolish leap seconds, allowing UTC to drift an hour
science.summary: Delegates from 69 countries voted at a meeting in Versailles on Oct. 15 to stop adding leap seconds to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), the world’s atomic-clock time standard. The change takes effect May 20, 2027, after which UTC may drift by as much as one hour from time based on Earth’s rotation before a correction
science.content: Delegates from 69 countries voted at a meeting in Versailles on Oct. 15 to stop adding leap seconds to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC), the world’s atomic-clock time standard. The change takes effect May 20, 2027, after which UTC may drift by as much as one hour from time based on Earth’s rotation before a correction is made. Leap seconds kept the two time scales close, but irregular 61-second minutes have disrupted digital services and networks that depend on precise synchronization. Earth’s recent increase in rotational speed also raised the possibility of subtracting a second for the first time, a change whose effects on software have not been tested. The new rule allows the gap to accumulate over a much longer period; experts say an hour-long correction is not expected for many centuries.
science.image_alt: Global timekeepers abolish leap seconds, allowing UTC to drift an hour

science.title: Nebula image depicts Sun’s future as neutrinos may shape stellar deaths
science.summary: Nautilus presents a nebula image as a view of how the Sun will eventually die, while a separate report from Universe Today says neutrino flavor may affect how a large star ends its life. Nautilus says the nebula’s light show lasts 25,000 years. Universe Today’s report links neutrino flavor to the fate of a large star.
science.content: Nautilus presents a nebula image as a view of how the Sun will eventually die, while a separate report from Universe Today says neutrino flavor may affect how a large star ends its life. Nautilus says the nebula’s light show lasts 25,000 years. Universe Today’s report links neutrino flavor to the fate of a large star.

science.title: Google cuts quantum state-preparation errors 40-fold on Willow
science.summary: Google researchers demonstrated a technique called magic-state cultivation on the company’s Willow quantum processor, reducing preparation errors about 40-fold and producing T-states with a reported logical fidelity of 99.99%. Magic states enable certain operations needed for complex quantum calculations, but preparing
science.content: Google researchers demonstrated a technique called magic-state cultivation on the company’s Willow quantum processor, reducing preparation errors about 40-fold and producing T-states with a reported logical fidelity of 99.99%. Magic states enable certain operations needed for complex quantum calculations, but preparing them reliably can consume substantial hardware and processing capacity. Estimates cited by Google put that burden as high as 95% of a future computer’s capacity. The method checks a state prepared in a small group of qubits and discards attempts that fail, keeping only those that pass. In the most stringent runs, the team retained about 8% of attempts. Researchers also transferred cultivated states between two error-correcting codes but reported that storage errors in one test exceeded simulation predictions. Google says larger-scale demonstrations and improvements in storing and using the states remain necessary before practical use in quantum computing.
science.image_alt: Google cuts quantum state-preparation errors 40-fold on Willow

science.title: Century-old Isle of Wight fossil identified as Europe
science.summary: Researchers identified a century-old skull fragment in London’s Natural History Museum as Invictibellatrix amberina, a previously unknown predatory dinosaur that lived about 120 million years ago on what is now the Isle of Wight. The study, published Oct. 14 in Royal Society Open Science, identifies the first confirmed
science.content: Researchers identified a century-old skull fragment in London’s Natural History Museum as Invictibellatrix amberina, a previously unknown predatory dinosaur that lived about 120 million years ago on what is now the Isle of Wight. The study, published Oct. 14 in Royal Society Open Science, identifies the first confirmed megaraptoran fossil in Europe and supports a proposed route for the group’s spread from Asia toward the southern supercontinent Gondwana. The fossil was found in 1924 and remained in the museum collection until researchers re-examined it using CT scans and evolutionary analyses. Those analyses suggest the species’ ancestors reached Europe from Asia around 130 million years ago and may have moved onward through land connections, although the exact route remains unknown. The skull fragment does not preserve the animal’s arms or claws, and the researchers said further fossils may help explain why megaraptors later disappeared from northern regions.
science.image_alt: Century-old Isle of Wight fossil identified as Europe

science.title: UN climate panel meeting ends without agreement on report timeline
science.summary: The UN climate panel (IPCC) ended a meeting without agreeing on a timeline for a major global climate review, according to a Reuters headline included in the Climate Home News source description. A France 24 headline in the same description also said the panel failed to agree on a date, citing an envoy. The review's pu
science.content: The UN climate panel (IPCC) ended a meeting without agreeing on a timeline for a major global climate review, according to a Reuters headline included in the Climate Home News source description. A France 24 headline in the same description also said the panel failed to agree on a date, citing an envoy. The review's publication schedule remains unsettled. A separate Earth.com article describes global warming and climate change as closely connected phenomena that scientists track separately. The Climate Home News article focused on who shapes climate science and on equity.
science.image_alt: UN climate panel meeting ends without agreement on report timeline

sports.title: NFL makes Packers running back Josh Jacobs eligible for Oct. 25 return
sports.summary: The National Football League will remove Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs from its Commissioner Exempt List on Monday, Oct. 19, making him eligible to play when the Packers visit the Detroit Lions on Oct. 25. He will miss Sunday’s game against the Dallas Cowboys after sitting out Green Bay’s first five games;
sports.content: The National Football League will remove Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs from its Commissioner Exempt List on Monday, Oct. 19, making him eligible to play when the Packers visit the Detroit Lions on Oct. 25. He will miss Sunday’s game against the Dallas Cowboys after sitting out Green Bay’s first five games; eligibility does not guarantee that he will play. The NFL said its investigation under the personal conduct policy remains open and could still lead to further discipline. Jacobs pleaded no contest on Sept. 10 to misdemeanor battery and property-damage charges stemming from a May altercation at his Wisconsin home. He received a $1,000 fine for battery. The property-damage charge can be dismissed after a year if he meets conditions including counseling and restitution.
sports.image_alt: NFL makes Packers running back Josh Jacobs eligible for Oct. 25 return

sports.title: England embrace underdog role for World Cup opener against Tonga
sports.summary: England captain George Williams says his side will embrace the underdog tag when they open their Rugby League World Cup campaign against Tonga in Perth on Saturday, October 17. Under the tournament format, England are expected to compete with Tonga, Samoa and Papua New Guinea for two remaining semi-final places, with A
sports.content: England captain George Williams says his side will embrace the underdog tag when they open their Rugby League World Cup campaign against Tonga in Perth on Saturday, October 17. Under the tournament format, England are expected to compete with Tonga, Samoa and Papua New Guinea for two remaining semi-final places, with Australia and New Zealand considered likely to advance from Pool A. Coach Brian McDermott has promised a different attacking approach after England’s 3-0 Ashes loss to Australia in 2025, and Williams says the squad has bought into the plan. Luke Thompson replaces the absent Morgan Knowles in a late lineup change, while Morgan Smithies has withdrawn through injury. Humidity at HBF Park is expected to exceed 60%. Williams described Tonga as packed with National Rugby League (NRL) talent.
sports.image_alt: England embrace underdog role for World Cup opener against Tonga

sports.title: Lions lock Hyron Andrews dies before club’s Champions Cup debut
sports.summary: South African rugby lock Hyron Andrews died at the Johannesburg Lions’ team hotel in France on Friday, October 16, aged 31, the day before the club’s scheduled Champions Cup match against La Rochelle. The South African Rugby Union said he died after an accidental fall. French authorities opened an investigation, and an
sports.content: South African rugby lock Hyron Andrews died at the Johannesburg Lions’ team hotel in France on Friday, October 16, aged 31, the day before the club’s scheduled Champions Cup match against La Rochelle. The South African Rugby Union said he died after an accidental fall. French authorities opened an investigation, and an autopsy was expected as they worked to establish the circumstances. The Lions chose to play the October 17 fixture in Andrews’ honour. It would be their first appearance in Europe’s top club competition. Organisers said a moment of silence would be held before every Champions Cup and Challenge Cup match that weekend. Andrews had returned to South Africa after playing for the Durban-based Sharks and England’s Sale Sharks. He made 45 appearances for Sale and represented South Africa’s Junior Springboks in 2015. Former clubs, rugby officials and teammates paid tribute to him, while support was arranged for Lions players and hotel staff.
sports.image_alt: Lions lock Hyron Andrews dies before club’s Champions Cup debut

sports.title: Ravens rule out Lamar Jackson, turn to Huntley against Browns

sports.content: The Baltimore Ravens ruled out two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson for Sunday’s game at the Cleveland Browns, leaving backup Tyler Huntley to make his second consecutive start. Jackson sprained his left ankle while being sacked in Baltimore’s Oct. 4 win over Tennessee and has not practiced since; Ravens coach Jesse Minter described his status as “day by day”. Huntley led the Ravens to a 30-23 overtime win over Atlanta last Sunday, throwing for 201 yards and two touchdowns as Baltimore improved to 4-1. He will face a Cleveland defense that has recorded 16 sacks. Baltimore will also be without center Cam Jurgens, tight end Matthew Hibner and defensive tackle Broderick Washington. The Ravens-Browns game is scheduled for Sunday, Oct. 18.

sports.content: Liverpool are emerging as frontrunners to sign Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott. The club believe new head coach Andoni Iraola’s previous work with the 23-year-old could give them an advantage in the January transfer race. Bournemouth are reportedly prepared to consider an offer above £100 million but are under no obligation to sell. Scott has rejected Bournemouth’s latest contract offer, and Chelsea remain interested after pursuing him in the summer. Liverpool are assessing the cost but have not committed to a move. Bournemouth’s stance could also depend on their league position, with one report saying they would consider a sale if Premier League safety appeared likely and they received a £100 million offer.

sports.content: The Denver Broncos opened NFL Week 6 by beating the Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime on Thursday, leaving 13 games on the schedule for Sunday and Monday. Sunday’s slate includes a meeting between AFC North rivals Baltimore and Cleveland, while the Houston Texans face the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium in London. The week concludes Monday night with the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers hosting Washington. Baltimore quarterback Lamar Jackson has been ruled out with an ankle injury, and Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts is out with a blood clot in his calf. The Eagles face Carolina on Sunday, while Baltimore visits Cleveland with first place in the AFC North at stake.

sports.content: Jonathan Milan won the men’s individual pursuit world title at the 2026 track cycling world championships in Shanghai, beating Frederik Rodenberg after breaking his own world record in qualifying. Great Britain also won two golds on day three, with Scottish rider Mark Stewart taking the men’s points race and Welsh rider Anna Morris winning the women’s omnium. Stewart beat Olympic omnium champion Benjamin Thomas by seven points, while Portugal’s Carlos Salgueiro took bronze. Morris, who had won women’s team pursuit gold on Thursday, beat Japan’s Tsuyaka Uchino and Denmark’s Amalie Dideriksen. Defending omnium champion Lorena Wiebes crashed in the opening scratch race and left the event. Britain also won silver through Emma Finucane in the women’s sprint and bronze through Joseph Truman in the men’s time trial.

sports.content: The WNBA Finals begin Saturday, Oct. 17, with the Golden State Valkyries hosting the Atlanta Dream at San Francisco’s Chase Center in a best-of-seven series between two teams seeking their first championship. Golden State, in its second season, reached the Finals by sweeping the defending champion Las Vegas Aces; Atlanta swept the New York Liberty to reach its first Finals since 2013. The Valkyries won all three regular-season meetings, but Atlanta’s rebounding and forward Angel Reese’s expanded shooting range give the Dream additional ways to challenge Golden State’s defense. Atlanta guard Allisha Gray, who missed the final two semifinal games with a hand injury, practiced Friday, but coach Karl Smesko said a decision on her availability would come near tipoff. Game 2 is scheduled for Monday in San Francisco; the series could run through Oct. 31 if it reaches seven games.
